title: The Crooked Veil Anew
premise: In the city of Vessengard, where the Concord outlawed magic a generation ago, Silas Okafor has served out her family's debt as a temple scribe, selling harmless charms to keep her head down. When prayers start being answered by gods everyone believed dead, Silas discovers she is a 'veilkeeper' — one of the few who can hear them — and the Concord's inquisitors want her either leashed or dead. Hunted alongside a disgraced inquisitor, Adric Vale, whose duty and growing love for her war against each other, she learns the old gods were never destroyed but locked behind a door in a country that was erased from maps. To free them — and herself — Silas must find that door before the long winter seals it for another century, choosing at last between the safety of belonging to no one and the peril of belonging to something. She opens the door at terrible cost: magic returns lawless to the world, Adric breaks with the Concord to stand beside her, and Silas, debt paid in blood rather than coin, walks into a country that exists again.
about_author: Theo Delacroix is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people caught between institutions and the truths those institutions buried.

chapters.title: Small Charms
chapters.summary: Silas Okafor's POV. We meet Silas in the night market of Vessengard, selling legal trinkets and illegal blessings, twelve years into a debt that owns her name. A dying beggar's whispered prayer is answered — impossibly — by a god with no temple. Emotional beat: weary caution cracked open by wonder.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Adric Vale's POV. Adric, a Concord inquisitor quietly doubting his order, is assigned to trace the miracle at the market. His investigation leads him to Silas's stall and a ledger entry bearing her family name from the old purge. Emotional beat: duty sharpening into obsession he doesn't yet understand.

chapters.title: What the Gods Remember
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The old god, Ashen-Mother, speaks through Silas, naming her a veilkeeper and showing her visions of a door in a drowned country called Ilvaren — erased from every map. The Concord raids her tenement; she flees with nothing but a stolen relic. Emotional beat: terror giving way to reluctant purpose.

chapters.title: Uneasy Custody
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Adric catches Silas but hesitates to turn her in, instead moving her through the city under pretense of custody. Their wary alliance forms over shared doubts about the Concord's founding lies. Emotional beat: two lonely people discovering they are not alone.

chapters.title: The Debt Collectors
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The temple that holds Silas's debt sells her contract to the Concord, making her flight theft of herself. Her old mentor betrays her location for absolution, forcing a brutal escape across the frozen river districts. Emotional beat: grief for the life of small compromises she can never return to.

chapters.title: Maps of Nowhere
chapters.summary: Adric's POV. Adric burns his own career to forge travel papers, following cartographers' rumors to the coast where Ilvaren supposedly sank. He confronts his superior, High Inquisitor Serane, and learns the Concord has known the gods lived all along. Emotional beat: disillusionment hardening into treason.

chapters.title: The Drowned Country
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. On the grey coast, Silas finds Ilvaren is not sunk but veiled — a whole nation folded out of the world when the Concord sealed the door. Inside its borders, time pools strangely, and the exiled gods gather like storm clouds. Emotional beat: awe shadowed by the scale of what was taken.

chapters.title: Winter's Bargain
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The long winter begins falling early — the Concord's final weapon to freeze the door shut forever. The gods offer Silas freedom and power if she opens the door alone; Adric begs her to run with him instead. Emotional beat: love against duty reaching its breaking point.

chapters.title: The Door Out
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, climax. Serane's inquisitors storm the veiled country as Silas reaches the door. Opening it requires a debt paid in full — and Silas pays it with her bound years, unmaking the contract that owned her. The veil tears; Ilvaren floods back into the world amid fire and snow. Emotional beat: sacrifice transfigured into self-ownership.

chapters.title: Anew
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, resolution. Magic returns lawless to Vessengard; the Concord fractures, Serane falls, and Adric publicly breaks his oath to stand with Silas. In the restored hills of Ilvaren, Silas plants a new temple with no debts attached. Emotional beat: quiet, earned belonging — justice outside the law, love chosen over duty.
